fullPassage:
[P01] A familiar song can remain interesting even when listeners know most of its melody. Their knowledge of familiar patterns gives them expectations that a performer can either satisfy or gently disturb. Suppose a singer repeats a short phrase several times and then holds its final note longer than before. The change feels meaningful partly because the earlier repetitions taught listeners when the note should end. Without that pattern, the extra length might not stand out at all. This helps explain why musical surprise is different from a collection of unrelated sounds. A surprise needs an expectation to depart from, while a completely unpredictable sequence offers little basis for anticipation. On the other hand, a performance that follows every expectation exactly may soon feel mechanical. An effective balance between these extremes creates emotional interest. The performer establishes enough order for the audience to follow, then introduces unexpected changes that make them listen more closely. The emotional value of music therefore depends not simply on the presence of something new, but on the relationship between what happens and what they were prepared to hear.

[P02] A business does not always reduce costs by using less of every resource. An effective business often makes changes to the balance of resources it uses. Imagine two small furniture companies that make similar tables. One operates in a town where workshop space is inexpensive, while the other works in a city where rent is high. The first company can afford to keep large supplies of wood and finished tables on site. The second may order materials more frequently and produce tables only after customers request them. This approach could increase delivery costs and require more careful planning. Nevertheless, it may be cheaper overall because it reduces the amount of costly space the company needs. What looks inefficient when one expense is considered alone can be efficient when all expenses are compared. There is therefore no single arrangement that is best for every business in every place. The value of an arrangement depends on the relationship between local prices and total costs. When one resource becomes expensive, a successful business may use more of another to achieve the same result at a lower total cost.

[P03] Free time may seem like something people obtain only after they become wealthy. However, it can also emerge when they become more effective at meeting basic needs. Imagine an early human group whose members search for food separately. Each person must discover where food is available and face the risks of collecting it. If they begin sharing information, watching seasonal changes, and dividing tasks, the same amount of food may require fewer hours of effort. Their advantage comes from organizing knowledge rather than simply increasing physical strength. Under favorable conditions, the time saved can be spent making tools, telling stories, or playing with children. Such activities are possible because survival no longer demands every available moment. This freedom is not guaranteed: a shortage of food can quickly consume it again. Still, the example shows why material abundance alone does not fully explain leisure. A group can gain time by changing how it works, even without greatly increasing what it owns. Greater intelligence and cooperation can therefore create opportunities that constant individual effort cannot.

[P04] During a frightening event, silence may occur before a person has consciously decided to remain quiet. A sudden unfamiliar noise can cause someone to stop moving, listen closely, and find speaking unexpectedly difficult. These reactions can be understood as parts of a protective response. Movement and sound might reveal a person's location, while stillness allows attention to be directed toward possible danger. From this perspective, the temporary loss of words is not necessarily a failure of language ability. A system concerned with immediate safety is interrupting an activity that might make the person easier to notice. Once the surroundings seem safe, movement and conversation can return. The difficulty arises when the sense of danger continues after the immediate threat has passed. A response that helps someone through a brief emergency may interfere with ordinary life if it remains active. Understanding this difference matters when we judge another person's silence. The question is not only whether that person knows what to say, but also whether their body currently allows them to say it.

det.korean: 비싼 공간을 줄이므로 전체적으로 '더 저렴(cheaper)'하다는 맥락이어서 ③ costlier(더 비싼)는 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ costlier 가 부적절 — 바로 뒤에 '비싼 공간을 줄인다'고 했으므로 전체적으로 '더 저렴(cheaper)'해야 한다.
❌ ① reduce : 비용을 '줄인다'는 핵심 맥락에 맞다.
❌ ② afford : 큰 재고를 '둘 여유가 있다'는 맥락에 맞다.
❌ ④ expensive : 한 자원이 '비싸질' 때라는 맥락에 맞다.
det.tip: 비싼 공간을 줄이므로 cheaper(더 저렴)가 맞다.

주변이 안전해 보이면 움직임과 대화가 돌아올 수 있다.
위협이 지나가면 위험에 대한 느낌은 항상 즉시 사라진다.

This helps explain why musical surprise is different from a collection of unrelated sounds. A surprise needs an expectation to depart from, while a completely unpredictable sequence offers little basis for anticipation. On the other hand, a performance that follows every expectation exactly may soon feel mechanical. An effective balance between these extremes creates emotional interest. The performer establishes enough order for the audience to follow, then introduces unexpected changes that make them listen more closely. The emotional value of music therefore depends not simply on the presence of something new, but on the relationship between what happens and what they were prepared to hear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 익숙한 노래는 멜로디를 대부분 알아도 흥미로울 수 있다.
완전히 예측 불가능한 소리의 연속이 가장 풍부한 감정적 가치를 지닌다.
모든 기대를 그대로 따르는 연주는 기계적으로 느껴질 수 있다.

det.korean: 완전히 예측 불가능한 연속은 기대의 근거가 거의 없다고 했으므로 ②는 본문과 다르다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 가 불일치 — 본문은 완전히 예측 불가능한 연속이 '기대의 근거를 거의 주지 못한다'고 하므로, 그것이 '가장 풍부한 감정적 가치'를 지닌다는 것은 틀리다.
❌ ① 일치 : A familiar song can remain interesting.
❌ ③ 일치 : A surprise needs an expectation to depart from.
❌ ④ 일치 : a performance that follows every expectation exactly may soon feel mechanical.

questions.passage: Imagine two small furniture companies that ① makes similar tables. One ② operates in a town where workshop space is inexpensive. The first company can ③ afford to keep large supplies of wood and finished tables. The second may ④ produce tables only after customers request them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: makes → make : 선행사 companies(복수)를 받는 주격 관계절 동사이므로 make로 써야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① makes 가 틀림 — 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 'companies'(복수)이므로 관계절 동사는 make여야 한다.
❌ ② operates : 주어 One(단수)에 맞는 동사로 맞다.
❌ ③ afford : 조동사 can 뒤 동사원형으로 맞다.
❌ ④ produce : 조동사 may 뒤 동사원형으로 맞다.

questions.passage: Free time may seem like something people obtain only after they become wealthy. However, it can also emerge when they become more effective at meeting basic needs. Imagine an early human group whose members search for food separately. Each person must discover where food is available and face the risks of collecting it. If they begin sharing information, watching seasonal changes, and dividing tasks, the same amount of food may require fewer hours of effort. Their advantage comes from organizing knowledge rather than simply increasing physical strength. Under favorable conditions, the time saved can be spent making tools, telling stories, or playing with children. Such activities are possible because survival no longer demands every available moment. This freedom is not guaranteed: a shortage of food can quickly consume it again. Still, the example shows why material abundance alone does not fully explain leisure. A group can gain time by changing how it works, even without greatly increasing what it owns. Greater intelligence and cooperation can therefore create opportunities that constant individual effort cannot.
questions.stem:
다음 질문에 대한 답이 되는 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (영어로)
Q: According to the passage, what can greater intelligence and cooperation create that constant individual effort cannot?
→ They can create __________.

det.korean: 마지막 문장에서 지능과 협력이 '기회(opportunities)'를 만들어 낸다고 했다.
det.analysis: 본문 'Greater intelligence and cooperation can therefore create opportunities that constant individual effort cannot'에서 핵심 목적어는 opportunities이다.

questions.passage: During a frightening event, silence may occur before a person has consciously decided to remain quiet. A sudden unfamiliar noise can cause someone to stop moving, listen closely, and find speaking unexpectedly difficult. These reactions can be understood as parts of a protective response. Movement and sound might reveal a person's location, while stillness allows attention to be directed toward possible danger. From this perspective, the temporary loss of words is not necessarily a failure of language ability. A system concerned with immediate safety is interrupting an activity that might make the person easier to notice. Once the surroundings seem safe, movement and conversation can return. The difficulty arises when the sense of danger continues after the immediate threat has passed. A response that helps someone through a brief emergency may interfere with ordinary life if it remains active. Understanding this difference matters when we judge another person's silence. The question is not only whether that person knows what to say, but also whether their body currently allows them to say it.
questions.stem: 공포 상황에서 멈춤과 침묵을 설명하는, 즉각적 안전을 위한 '몸의 반응'을 가리키는 2단어 영어 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 본문은 멈춤·침묵을 '보호 반응(protective response)'의 일부로 설명한다.
det.analysis: 본문 'These reactions can be understood as parts of a protective response'에서 2단어 표현은 protective response이다.

questions.passage: An effective balance between these extremes creates emotional interest. The performer establishes enough order for the audience to follow, then __________ (introduce) unexpected changes that make them listen more closely.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 주어 The performer(3인칭 단수)에 맞춰 현재시제 introduces로 쓴다.
det.analysis: 주어 'The performer'는 3인칭 단수이고 앞의 establishes와 병렬되는 현재동사이므로 introduce → introduces.

questions.passage: A business does not always reduce costs by using less of every resource. An effective business often makes changes to the balance of resources it uses. Imagine two small furniture companies that make similar tables. One operates in a town where workshop space is inexpensive, while the other works in a city where rent is high. The first company can afford to keep large supplies of wood and finished tables on site. The second may order materials more frequently and produce tables only after customers request them. This approach could increase delivery costs and require more careful planning. Nevertheless, it may be cheaper overall because it reduces the amount of costly space the company needs. What looks inefficient when one expense is considered alone can be efficient when all expenses are compared. There is therefore no single arrangement that is best for every business in every place. The value of an arrangement depends on the relationship between local prices and total costs. When one resource becomes expensive, a successful business may use more of another to achieve the same result at a lower total cost.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 비용을 줄이려면 항상 모든 자원을 더 적게 써야 한다.
가구 회사는 반드시 대도시에 위치해야 한다.
비용 절감은 모든 자원을 덜 쓰는 것이 아니라 지역 여건에 맞춘 자원 배분에 달려 있다.
좋은 가구를 만들려면 넓은 작업 공간이 반드시 필요하다.

det.korean: 비용 절감은 모든 자원을 덜 쓰는 것이 아니라 지역 가격에 맞춰 자원 배분을 바꾸는 데서 온다는 것이 요지이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 이 요지 — 본문은 '모든 자원을 덜 쓴다고 비용이 주는 것이 아니라' 지역 여건(가격)에 맞춰 자원 구성을 바꾸는 것이 핵심이라고 한다.
❌ ① 본문은 '항상 더 적게'를 부정한다.
❌ ② 도시/시골은 예시일 뿐 필수 조건이 아니다.
❌ ④ 넓은 공간이 필수라는 말은 없다.
det.tip: 핵심어 = balance of resources, local prices.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 지식의 조직과 협력을 통해 생겨나는 여가
부가 늘어날수록 자동으로 늘어나는 여가 시간
초기 인류가 사냥 중 겪은 위험들

det.korean: 여가는 부가 아니라 지식을 조직하고 협력함으로써 생겨날 수 있다는 것이 주제이다.
det.analysis:

❌ ② 본문은 부(물질적 풍요)만으로는 여가를 설명할 수 없다고 한다.
❌ ③ 위험은 예시의 일부일 뿐 주제가 아니다.
❌ ④ 신체적 힘 기르기는 오히려 본문이 부정하는 방향이다.
